Author: K.R. Mohapatra
Bench: K.R. Mohapatra
 W.P.(C) No.25084 of 2020
 W.P.(C) No.25084 of 2020 &
 I.A. No. 11180 of 2020
3. 07.10.2020

Due to outbreak of Covid-19, this matter is
 taken up through Video Conferencing.
Heard R.K. Mohanty, learned Senior Advocate  along with Mr. Vivekananda Jena, learned counsel for  the petitioner and Mr. A.K. Bose, learned Assistant  Solicitor General for the opposite party No.1.

The petitioner in this writ petition assails the  action of the opposite parties in issuing the letter dated  23.09.2020 (Annexure-1) issued by the Advisor (Science  and Standards), Food Safety and Standards Authority of  India and the letter dated 25.09.2020 (Annexure-2)
 issued by the Deputy Director/Central Licensing  Authority, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India-  opposite No.2, requesting the petitioner to refrain from  all the activities, such as, manufactureing, repacking  trading selling, storing of Blended, Edible Vegetable Oil  with Mustard Oil with effect from 01st October, 2020.
 Mr. Mohanty, learned Senior Advocate for the  petitioner submits that on the basis of a draft notification  namely, the Draft Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition  and Restrictions on Sales) Amendment Regulations,
 2020, the letters under Annexures-1 and 2 have been  issued.

But, in absence of any  2 law to that effect the authorities under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India have no jurisdiction to issue such letters.

Notice of this Court is drawn to the order passed by the Delhi High Court in W.P.(C) No.7217/2020 on the subject matter of the dispute, wherein Court prima facie accepted the WP(C)/25084/2020 on 7 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68624199/
1 submission of learned counsel for the petitioner therein,
who placed reliance upon the judgment dated 30.06.2014 passed by the Bombay High Court in W.P.(C)
No. 2746 of 2013 in the case of Vital Nutraceuticals Pvt.
Ltd. & Another -v- Union of India & Another, wherein it is held that the provision of Sections 92 and 93 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 cannot be circumvented by the opposite parties on the basis of a draft notification.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the Delhi High Court vide order dated 29.09.2020 has granted stay of the order prohibiting the lawful activities of manufacturing,
repacking trading selling, storing of such Blended, Edible Vegetable Oil with Mustard Oil.
He, therefore, prays for a direction to stay operation of the letters under Annexures- 1 and 2.

Mr. Bose, learned Assistant Solicitor General for the opposite party No.1, on the other hand, submits  3 that the Central Government is competent to make the rules and issue notification for regulating the Food Safety and Standards.
Accordingly, a draft notification has been issued prohibiting blending of edible vegetable oil with mustard oil.
It is clearly stated therein that it will be effective from 1st October, 2020.
Accordingly, Annexures- 1 & 2 have been issued.
He, however, submits that he will take instructions in the matter and file a detail counter affidavit.
Taking into consideration the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court feels that the matter requires consideration.
Issue notice.
Mr. Bose, learned Assistant Solicitor General accepts notice on behalf of opposite party No.1, an extra copy of the writ petition shall be served on him by 12th October, 2020.
Issue notice to opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 by speed post with A.D. fixing a short returnable date.
Requisites shall be filed by 12th October, 2020.
Put up this matter in the week commencing from 16th November, 2020.

In the meantime, there shall be stay operation of the letter dated 23.09.2020 under Annexure-1 issued by the Advisor (Science and Standards) and the letter dated 25.09.2020 under Annexure-2 issued by the Deputy  4  Director/Central Licensing Authority, Food Safety and  Standards Authority of India till the next date.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
The petitioner in this writ petition assails the  action of the opposite parties in issuing the letter dated  23.09.2020 (Annexure-1) issued by the Advisor (Science  and Standards), Food Safety and Standards Authority of  India and the letter dated 25.09.2020 (Annexure-2)
 issued by the Deputy Director/Central Licensing  Authority, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India-  opposite No.2, requesting the petitioner to refrain from  all the activities, such as, manufactureing, repacking  trading selling, storing of Blended, Edible Vegetable Oil  with Mustard Oil with effect from 01st October, 2020.
 Mr. Mohanty, learned Senior Advocate for the  petitioner submits that on the basis of a draft notification  namely, the Draft Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition  and Restrictions on Sales) Amendment Regulations,
 2020, the letters under Annexures-1 and 2 have been  issued.
It is further submitted that the authorities have  every right to put restrictions as detailed in Annexure-2  following due procedure of law.
But, in absence of any  2 law to that effect the authorities under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India have no jurisdiction to issue such letters.
They have purportedly acted under a draft notification which is per se illegal.
When no such notification has yet been issued, the authority could not have restricted the lawful activities of the petitioner under the umbrella a draft notification.
